story.what_it_does: Can Fin Homes is a housing finance company that lends mainly for home purchase. Its loan book was ₹42,209 crore at March 2026, up about 10%, and it reached ₹43,539 crore by September 2026. Canara Bank is its sponsor bank and a major lender to it.
story.plans: Management targets about ₹13,000 crore of disbursements and 13-14% loan book growth in FY27, with credit cost of about 10 bps. It also wants more direct sourcing, a larger share of self-employed and non-professional (SENP) borrowers, more branches and a bigger sales team. The new IT system (Project Tejas) was completed across all branches by October 1, 2026.
story.moat: The notes show a low gross NPA (0.85% in FY26), a net interest margin of 3.93% and a return on assets of 2.58%, which suggest tight cost control and good credit discipline. Its sponsor bank, Canara Bank, supplies funding and has a related-party limit of ₹4,857 crore. The notes do not describe a clear competitive edge, and pricing competition is raising prepayments.

scenarios.story: The IT migration is finished and disbursements recover toward the Q3 target of ₹3,500 crore, so loan growth moves toward the 13-14% goal. Asset quality stays clean and credit cost stays near 10 bps.
signals_to_watch: Q3 FY27 disbursements against the ₹3,500 crore target
Run-down (prepayment) ratio, which was 4.40% in Q1 FY27

scenarios.story: Growth stays near 10% as higher prepayments offset new lending, and margins hover around 3.8-3.9%. Profit keeps growing at a modest pace with stable asset quality.
signals_to_watch: Net interest margin versus the 3.75% guidance, with Q2 FY27 at 3.89%
Loan book growth year on year, about 10% in Q2 FY27

scenarios.story: Borrowing costs rise faster than lending rates, and prepayments keep eating into the loan book while weak rains slow demand. Margins narrow and delinquencies build further.
signals_to_watch: Delinquency pool, which rose to 8.41% in Q2 FY27
Cost of funds, 7.03% in Q2 FY27, and new-loan bank borrowing costs of about 7.25-7.5%
